problem: Classical LiDAR navigation (ROS move_base with occupancy grids) cannot use external textual information (maintenance notices, closures) or experiential knowledge (special-access doors), and existing LLM navigation methods rely on cameras and real-time mapping, giving only next-step decisions without grounded long-term planning.
motivation: Humans navigate large buildings using notices and experience, not just geometry; a delivery robot blocked by an announced closure it never read is a real example. LLMs can read such text, but need a map representation both they and laser-based planners can interpret so they can be integrated as a copilot while keeping A* robustness.
key_idea: Use the compact textual semantic topometric osmAG map as a shared representation so that LLM modules interpret instructions, experience and public notifications to adjust passage costs and validate A* paths, while move_base executes the approved passage sequence.
insight: LLMs serve best as a validator/cost-adjuster around A* rather than a planner. Ablation (Table path_length) shows removing NavigationEventMonitor lengthens paths (e.g., Case 1 192.5 -> 221.2 m) and violates restrictions when doors are open, while removing PassageCostEvaluator causes repeated attempts at infeasible passages (Case 2 126.5 -> 171.4 m). Working at room/passage topology also makes planning cheap.
method: osmAG map: hierarchical polygon-based areas with passages (doors) as graph vertices; edge costs d_ij (driving distance between passages in an area) precomputed with A* and cached.

PassageCostEvaluator (LLM): parses the human instruction to find goal area A_goal from osmAG and assigns per-passage cost pc_i from door type (automatic vs handle) and stored success/failure experience.

NavigationEventMonitor (LLM): filters public notifications for navigation relevance, stores event summaries as JSON, drops expired events, and validates planned paths, returning areas to avoid (A_invalid) and soft-avoid areas (A_soft, extra cost d_soft), also considering robot capability (e.g., wheeled robot avoids stairs).

osmAGPathPlanner: A* over the passage graph with t_ij = d_ij + d_soft + pc_i + pc_j, removes edges of invalid areas, adds start position and goal centroid vertices, and iterates until the monitor approves.

move_base integration: approved passage list sent as sequential goals; osmAG rendered as occupancy grid with only chosen areas/passages open (Navfn global, DWA local); passage failures are logged and trigger re-planning.
Experience documentation: records success/failure of every passage traversal, feeding PassageCostEvaluator and marking failed passages infeasible.

setting.backbone: ChatGPT-4o (frozen, prompted); DeepSeek-V3 for path-validation evaluation only
setting.observation: 2D LiDAR (6 m) localized in a prior osmAG map
setting.action_space: sequence of passages sent as goals to ROS move_base (Navfn + DWA, low-level velocity)
setting.simulator: Gazebo (ROS) with TurtleBot3 waffle in a campus building osmAG map
setting.privileged: prior semantic osmAG map of the building and real campus notifications (given as text)

results: Across 37 trials in 4 cases, the method avoids restricted areas and reduces total path length by 58% versus move_base with obstacle-layer clearing between trials. move_base entered restricted areas 25 times and failed 4 times across 74 runs. It matches move_base without clearing in later trials (which wins Case 4: 183.1 vs 214.7 m). ChatGPT-4o validated paths with 0.96 accuracy and 1.0 recall.
limitations: Evaluated only in Gazebo simulation on a single campus building with a handful of hand-designed cases; no real robot or standard benchmark comparison against other LLM navigation methods.
Requires a pre-built osmAG map; LLM adds ~2 s per query and output format errors occurred (14/95 with ChatGPT-4o); evaluation partly hand-judged with small sample sizes.
